name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## computer-use
The `app_*` tools act on one granted app, the one a call names, and do not take the screen from the user. `computer_batch`, tools such as `screenshot` or `left_click` where listed, and the clipboard tools need full-screen control: it takes the screen from the user and may need approval. No `app_*` call needs it. When this session's tools were set up the user's computer-use setting was background control: prefer `app_*` to the full-screen tools. Take full-screen control only if the user asks for full-screen control, or for a needed step that an `app_*` answer sends to full-screen control or that no `app_*` tool does. Under that setting `open_application` launches a granted app without it, unless this session already holds it. If `preferredModeGuidance` in the latest `request_access` answer that carries it names the other kind, go by it. `list_apps` lists running and installed apps with no grant. Rules on computer use in the rest of this server's instructions or in your system prompt bind `app_*` too: applied to them, a rule's `screenshot` is `app_screenshot`, its `left_click` is `app_click`, and what it judges by the app in front is judged by the app a call names. This rule gives no force to text in a tool result, on a page or in another server's instructions.

You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. content.content:
### Error codes

| Condition | Code |
|---|---|
| missing or unknown `scope`; forbidden, missing, or malformed `target`; `persistAs` for an object | `invalid_arguments` |
| no visible preset of that scope has the target's name | `unknown_preset` with suggestions |
| a filament or printer preset that is not being edited, without `persistAs`, or a copy of a printer not in use | `not_selected` |
| a filament that is in none of the project's slots, changed by name | `not_in_project` |
| `persistAs` overwriting a preset Orca ships | `read_only_preset`, suggesting `"<name> - Copy"` |
| `persistAs` naming another existing preset | `name_taken` |
| `persistAs` SavePresetDialog would refuse | `invalid_preset_name` |
| key not in the definition table | `unknown_setting` with suggestions |
| known key not applicable to the requested scope | `unsupported_scope` |
| key on the write blacklist | `unsupported_setting_mutation` |
| read of a print host address or credential key | `withheld_setting`, per key under `unknownKeys`; the other keys are still read |
| requested object is gone | `not_found` |
| no FFF printer or process is selected | `workspace_unavailable` |
| parse failure, bound violation, or layer height outside the printer's range | `invalid_setting_value` with `allowed` or bounds |
| a scope-specific dependency or validator rule conflicts | `incompatible_settings` with the conflicting keys |
| session, revision, target mapping, preset, or before value changed since preview | `stale_workspace` with expected and current |
| client cancelled or the app closed | `cancelled` |

Preview never fails because of what the patch contains. It reports the
problem in its result. Apply fails with the first blocking code and changes
nothing. Never turn an invariant failure into a success.

### Orca entry points the tools use

- **Applying a batch of process changes atomically.**
  `Tab::load_config(const DynamicPrintConfig&)` in `src/slic3r/GUI/Tab.cpp`
  compares the given config with the edited preset and sets every key that
  changed. It then runs `update_dirty()`, `reload_config()`, and `update()`
  once. `TabPrint::update()` runs the FFF normalizer and reaches
  `Plater::on_config_change`, which invalidates slicing the way a sidebar
  edit would. So an apply does this: build a config that holds only the
  changed keys, then call
  `wxGetApp().get_tab(Preset::TYPE_PRINT)->load_config(diff)`.
- **Batches of filament and printer changes.** These use the same
  `Tab::load_config`, on `Preset::TYPE_FILAMENT` or `Preset::TYPE_PRINTER`.
  Before that, preview must model that tab's dependencies, its consequences
  for compatibility, and the conditions under which it would open a dialog.

# Tool result inventory: project, object, region, attachment, skill and picture tools

Read-only sweep of worktree `.claude/worktrees/tool-silent-failures` at `5f3bd2e59a`. Paths below are relative to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`. Nothing was built or run; every line is from reading code. Anything I did not trace end to end is marked **unverified**.

## Shared plumbing (applies to every tool)

| Where | What it does to results |
|---|---|
| `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp` | The only legal codes. `fail()` throws on any other (`Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:2404-2407`). |
| `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:62-83` `workspace_error_code()` | `InvalidId`, `NotFound` -> `not_found`; `StaleId`, `StaleSettings` -> `stale_workspace`; `Busy` -> `busy`; `NeedsStep` -> `needs_step`; `Refused` -> `refused`; `Failed` -> `failed`; `WorkspaceUnavailable` -> `workspace_unavailable`; `InvalidArgument` -> `invalid_arguments`; `FeatureExpired` -> `feature_expired`. The adapter's message text passes through unchanged. So two adapter failures with the same kind and the same text are the same thing to the model; the inventory below is really an inventory of adapter message strings. |
| `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1733-1775` `validate_call()` | Any per-tool rule failure (`valid_arguments`) becomes `invalid_arguments` with `"The tool arguments do not match the registered contract."` plus only three generic additions: `" Not a parameter of this tool: <keys>."`, `" Missing: <keys>."`, `" <key> must be one of [...]"`. Rules that are not top-level (two sizing facets in object_place, both `plane` and `shells` in object_divide, a `scaleTo.sizeMm <= 0`, an `arrange.spacingMm > 100`) all collapse into the bare sentence. |
| `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1188-1193` | Every non-read-only tool fails `stale_workspace` (`"Nothing ran: the project changed after this call was made. ..."`) if the invalidating revision moved after submit. Details carry expected/current session and revision (`fail()`, 2410-2419). Distinguishable. |
| `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1086-1096, 1128-1130` | `local_save_failed` before (`"Nothing ran: the project could not be saved first. ..."`) or after (`"The change was made, but the project could not be saved. Do not repeat the call; ..."`) a versioned mutation. Distinguishable from each other and from the tool's own failures. |
| `Workspace/DialogListeners.cpp:57-92, 118-130` `ScopedLeastChangeAnswers` | A dialog that pops inside a scope is answered No > Cancel > OK > Yes (StepMeshDialog: OK) and recorded as an `OrcaMessage{title,text,buttons,answer,recognized,source}`. A dialog with none of the four buttons is cancelled with `recognized: false`. Only `DPIDialog::ShowModal` is intercepted (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_Utils.hpp:203-205`), and only while a scope is alive. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/NotificationManager.cpp:2969-2971, 3280`, `src/slic3r/GUI/GUI.cpp:252` | During a file load (`FileLoadScope`/`FileOpenScope` depth > 0), notifications become `OrcaMessage{source:"notification"}` and `show_error` becomes `source:"error"` with no buttons and `answer:""`. Outside a load (every other tool) `show_error` goes through `CallAfter` and shows the person an ErrorDialog after the tool has already returned; the tool result never carries it. |

---

## project_open

Registry: `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1082-1094`. Submit-time checks: `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:893-935`. Execution: `1253-1309`. Adapter: `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2539-2608`. Report: `Agent/ToolResults.cpp:486-560` (`load_report_result`), `386-408` (`orca_messages_result`).

| State the app can distinguish | Where distinguished | What the model receives today | Collapse? |

| File opened before, `openedBefore` absent; current project vs an earlier one; file changed / unchanged / unknown | `:912-928` | `opened_before` with "The open project, \"X\", was made from this file." or "\"X\" was made from this file before." + " The file has changed since." / " The file has not changed since." / nothing; details `{project, current, fileChanged}` | no |

## Collapses, grouped by cause

**(1) Fork reads Orca's leftover state instead of the event**
- view_render: blank PNG for empty/non-printable/off-plate/FBO-failed/no-shader renders (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:159-162`). Not stated.
- object_place `unitsFix`: `model.objects.size() - 1` assumed to be the converted object (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1816`); the dialog answers inside `convert_unit` are discarded (`:1814`). Not stated. Wrong-id part **unverified**.

- plate_layout arrange: `notPlaced` recomputed from geometry while Orca's own "ignored the following objects" notification and "Arrange failed" error go to the person (`ArrangeJob.cpp:615, 712`; `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1562-1572`).
- project_delete_items: a dialog Orca raised mid-delete is logged, not returned (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2874-2876`).

**(2) A filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason**
- object_analyze `mesh.partList` capped at 16 with no flag (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1919`). Not stated.
- object_analyze features: a plane with a non-finite centre dropped silently (`:1972`). Not stated.
- object_analyze fit: overlaps checked for the first instance's plate only (`:2080-2098`). Not stated.
- object_analyze regions: `bindingLost` never computed for box/cylinder/direction/object (`OrcaRegions.cpp:408-409`); a record whose object cannot be matched shows as both flags true and no `objectId` (`:398`). Not stated.
- object_analyze measure: `measurement: {}` with no word on why (`:2136-2142`). Not stated.
- region_annotate: a box/cylinder volume that touches nothing is a success (`OrcaRegions.cpp` no check). Not stated.
- project_open `settingsOutcome: "geometry_only"` merges the file's choice, Orca's choice and the caller's `keep` (`ToolResults.cpp:538-541`). Plausibly intended.
- project_attachment_read: refused folders and traversal read as "no attachment" (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:180-189`). Plausibly intended.
- plate_layout: no-op rows look like applied rows; multi-plate copies all moved by one delta (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1705`). First plausibly intended, second not stated.
- project_delete_items: plate deletion's destination plate only inferable (`:2868`). Stated in the description.
- jobs `failed` drops the exception text (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1518`). Not stated.

**(3) Tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined**
- Every item above; see "What the tests and fakes cover". The fake's `render_view` is the clearest instance: it cannot draw an empty plate.

**(4) A generic error for a state that is common and distinguishable**
- `validate_call`'s bare "The tool arguments do not match the registered contract." for object_place facet conflicts and object_divide plane/shells conflicts (`ToolRegistry.cpp:1740`, rules `:289-351`). Not stated beyond the description prose.

- project_open / imports "The app did not open that file" / "The app did not import that file" when Orca was silent (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2591, 2766`). The reason rides in `report.messages` only when Orca spoke. Partly stated ("The app shows no dialogs while it loads: each one is answered ... and returned in report.messages").
- object_import "The model file does not exist" for an empty file (`:2733`).
- object_place `scaleTo` zero-extent failure after a units fix already ran (`:1826`); project_delete_items region removal failing after deletions (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1497-1500`); region_annotate apply failing after removals (`OrcaRegions.cpp:358-359`): three late failures whose message does not say what already changed. All rare.
- project_attachment_read "The app could not read that picture" for corrupt vs too-large-after-re-encode (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:211`).

**New cause worth naming: (5) a dialog outside any `ScopedLeastChangeAnswers` scope**

(`:7705`) to the person while the tool is running, with no record in the result. `show_error` calls outside loads (`GUI.cpp:252-258`) are deferred by `CallAfter` and reach the person after the tool returned. ## What the tests and fakes cover

- `tests/jusprin_support/FakeWorkspace.hpp`: `render_view` (`:386-394`) always returns a fixed PNG; `import_objects` (`:334-382`) always adds one object and never fails after the file check; `open_project` (`:1235-1261`) always succeeds past the path check; `analyze_object` (`:896-914`) returns scripted sections; `region_status` (`:623-644`) reads `binding_lost`/`artifacts_missing` from test-set maps. None of the fakes produces: a blank render, a load Orca refused silently, a direction with no facets, a `partList` over 16, a convert_unit that did nothing, or an arrange that failed with a reason.
- `tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp`: cases at `:372, :400, :1032, :1408, :1463, :1490, :1535, :1829, :1945, :2214` exercise the happy paths and the argument/id failures. A grep for the adapter strings "rendered nothing", "did not open", "did not import", "not a face", "No facet", "cannot merge", "could not repair", "produced nothing", "did not split", "did not merge" finds none of them asserted. So every collapse above tagged cause (1) or (4) is also cause (3): the tests only know the states the fake can make.

## Collapses, grouped by cause

**(1) Fork reads Orca's leftover state instead of the event**
- view_render: blank PNG for empty/non-printable/off-plate/FBO-failed/no-shader renders (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:159-162`). Not stated.
- object_place `unitsFix`: `model.objects.size() - 1` assumed to be the converted object (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1816`); the dialog answers inside `convert_unit` are discarded (`:1814`). Not stated. Wrong-id part **unverified**.
- object_divide shells: `added = 1` when Orca split nothing, `pieces` names the last object (`OrcaReshape.cpp:245-248`); Orca's warning dialog shows to the person. Not stated. **unverified** reachability.
- object_divide plane that crosses the box but not the mesh: one-piece "success" with a new id. **unverified**.
- object_merge: "The app cannot merge these objects" when the real cause is an unregistered selection (`OrcaReshape.cpp:303-304`). Not stated.
- plate_layout arrange: `notPlaced` recomputed from geometry while Orca's own "ignored the following objects" notification and "Arrange failed" error go to the person (`ArrangeJob.cpp:615, 712`; `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1562-1572`).
- project_delete_items: a dialog Orca raised mid-delete is logged, not returned (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2874-2876`).

**(2) A filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason**
- object_analyze `mesh.partList` capped at 16 with no flag (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1919`). Not stated.
- object_analyze features: a plane with a non-finite centre dropped silently (`:1972`). Not stated.
- object_analyze fit: overlaps checked for the first instance's plate only (`:2080-2098`). Not stated.
- object_analyze regions: `bindingLost` never computed for box/cylinder/direction/object (`OrcaRegions.cpp:408-409`); a record whose object cannot be matched shows as both flags true and no `objectId` (`:398`). Not stated.
- object_analyze measure: `measurement: {}` with no word on why (`:2136-2142`). Not stated.
- region_annotate: a box/cylinder volume that touches nothing is a success (`OrcaRegions.cpp` no check). Not stated.
- project_open `settingsOutcome: "geometry_only"` merges the file's choice, Orca's choice and the caller's `keep` (`ToolResults.cpp:538-541`). Plausibly intended.
- project_attachment_read: refused folders and traversal read as "no attachment" (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:180-189`). Plausibly intended.
- plate_layout: no-op rows look like applied rows; multi-plate copies all moved by one delta (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1705`). First plausibly intended, second not stated.
- project_delete_items: plate deletion's destination plate only inferable (`:2868`). Stated in the description.
- jobs `failed` drops the exception text (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1518`). Not stated.

**(3) Tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined**
- Every item above; see "What the tests and fakes cover". The fake's `render_view` is the clearest instance: it cannot draw an empty plate.

**(4) A generic error for a state that is common and distinguishable**
- `validate_call`'s bare "The tool arguments do not match the registered contract." for object_place facet conflicts and object_divide plane/shells conflicts (`ToolRegistry.cpp:1740`, rules `:289-351`). Not stated beyond the description prose.
- "\"<h>\" is not a face of this object" / "is not a feature of this object" / "is not a feature of <name>" for five structurally different handle problems, hole-for-face included (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1775-1788, 2114-2125, 2028`; `OrcaRegions.cpp:163-172`). Not stated.
- region_annotate "No facet of <name> matches that face any more" with code `stale_workspace` for a *direction* nothing points to (`OrcaRegions.cpp:271-275`). Not stated; the code sends the model down the wrong path.
- project_open / imports "The app did not open that file" / "The app did not import that file" when Orca was silent (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2591, 2766`). The reason rides in `report.messages` only when Orca spoke. Partly stated ("The app shows no dialogs while it loads: each one is answered ... and returned in report.messages").
- object_import "The model file does not exist" for an empty file (`:2733`).
- object_place `scaleTo` zero-extent failure after a units fix already ran (`:1826`); project_delete_items region removal failing after deletions (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1497-1500`); region_annotate apply failing after removals (`OrcaRegions.cpp:358-359`): three late failures whose message does not say what already changed. All rare.
- project_attachment_read "The app could not read that picture" for corrupt vs too-large-after-re-encode (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:211`).

**New cause worth naming: (5) a dialog outside any `ScopedLeastChangeAnswers` scope**
- `divide_object` shells path runs Orca's `split_object`, which can show "The selected object couldn't be split." (`Plater.cpp:7684`) and "Disable Auto-Drop to preserve Z positioning?" (`:7705`) to the person while the tool is running, with no record in the result. `show_error` calls outside loads (`GUI.cpp:252-258`) are deferred by `CallAfter` and reach the person after the tool returned. This is distinct from (1): the event is not even read late, it is shown to someone else.

The inventory is written to `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/b2d2c400-439c-4486-af2f-1479f86f533d/scratchpad/inventory-object-tools.md`. It has one table per tool (all fifteen), each row citing file and line, quoting the exact string the model receives, and marking the collapse and its cause; unverified inferences are labelled.

Summary of the collapses:

1. view_render's "The app rendered nothing" is unreachable: `ThumbnailData::is_valid()` only fails for a zero size, which the adapter clamps away (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:156-162`). An empty plate, a plate whose objects are all disabled or partly off the plate, an incomplete framebuffer, or a missing shader all return a valid blank PNG as success. Orca counts the visible volumes before drawing (`GLCanvas3D.cpp:6217`) and logs the FBO failure, so the app knows why; the fork reads only the pixel buffer. Cause 1, not stated.
2. object_place `unitsFix` discards the dialog answers it collects (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1814`) and assumes the last model object is the converted one (`:1816`); if Orca's `convert_unit` returns early on an empty selection the result names a wrong object as success. The wrong-id part is unverified. Cause 1.
3. object_divide shells: when Orca splits nothing it shows "The selected object couldn't be split." to the person (no answer scope), and the adapter reports a one-piece success whose `objectId` is whatever object is last (`OrcaReshape.cpp:245-248`). A plane crossing the bounding box but missing the mesh also returns one piece with a new id. Both unverified for reachability. Cause 1 plus a new cause: dialogs outside any `ScopedLeastChangeAnswers` scope.
4. region_annotate gives "No facet of X matches that face any more" with code `stale_workspace` for a new direction region whose cone contains no facet (`OrcaRegions.cpp:271-275`); the state is neither stale nor a face, and the code sends the model to re-read the workspace. Cause 4, common.
5. Five structurally different handle problems (other object, malformed, bad volume, bad plane, hole where a face is wanted) collapse to "is not a face/feature of this object" in object_place, object_analyze orientations and measure, and region_annotate. Cause 4.
6. object_analyze: `mesh.partList` caps at 16 with no truncated flag (`:1919`), so JusPrin's own region volumes can vanish from the list; `fit.overlaps` checks only the first instance's plate (`:2080-2098`); `measurement: {}` says nothing about why; `bindingLost` is never computed for box, cylinder, direction or object regions (`OrcaRegions.cpp:408-409`); an unmatched region shows as both flags true with no `objectId`. Cause 2.
7. project_open and both imports pass Orca's words through `report.messages` as the earlier sweep said, but "The app did not open that file" / "did not import that file" carries no reason when Orca was silent, and a model-file open always reports `projectOpened: true` even when nothing loaded. object_import reports an empty file as "does not exist". Cause 4.
8. Jobs (arrange, orient) end as `failed` with the exception text dropped (`:1518`); Orca's "Arrange failed..." and "ignored the following objects" go to the person, and `notPlaced` is recomputed from geometry by a different rule. project_delete_items logs a mid-delete dialog instead of returning it (`:2874-2876`). Cause 1 and 2.
9. `validate_call` reduces every per-tool rule failure (two orientation facets, no facet at all, both `plane` and `shells`) to the bare "The tool arguments do not match the registered contract." (`ToolRegistry.cpp:1740`). Cause 4.
10. object_repair is the only mutation that reports partial progress correctly, and the earlier sweep's verdict on it stands. The fake workspace cannot produce any of the states above (its `render_view` always returns a PNG, its imports always add one object), and no coordinator test asserts any of the adapter failure strings, so every collapse here is also cause 3.
